problems.text: diagonal angles: rectangle ABCD, E; angle ABD 27; find angle CAD
problems.explain: A rectangle’s diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so EA = EB = EC = ED, and each of the four small triangles is isosceles. △AEB is isosceles (EA = EB), so ∠ABD = ∠CAB; with ∠ABD = 27°, that makes ∠CAB = 27°. Then the corner at A is 90°, so ∠CAD = 90° − ∠CAB: ∠CAD = 90 − 27 = 63°. (The diagonal does not halve the right angle unless the rectangle is a square.) So ∠CAD = 63°.

problems.explain: In a kite the diagonal AC is a line of symmetry, so the angles between unequal sides match: ∠B = ∠D. All four add to 360°. So 7x + 37 = 9x + 23. Take 7x from both sides: 2x + 23 = 37; take away 23: 2x = 14; divide by 2: x = 7. Check: both come to 86°. (∠A is between the two equal sides; it is not one of the matching pair.) So x = 7.
